title: ranunculus retroflexus
intro: Ranunculus retroflexus, commonly known as poison ivy or poison oak, is a perennial plant with leaves that can cause severe skin irritation and allergic reactions in humans. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including reducing inflammation and pain, as well as its antiseptic and antiviral properties. The therapeutic actions of Ranunculus retroflexus include its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce fever, and treat skin conditions such as eczema and acne. The bioactive constituents of the plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential uses in treating various health conditions.
